content:
Using an Xbox Wireless Controller (Series X|S, USB‑C) with the official Microsoft USB dongle on Linux is not plug‑and‑play.
Unlike Bluetooth, the dongle requires runtime firmware and a user‑space daemon called xow.
This note documents the minimal, working setup that finally made it work.
Environment OS: Arch Linux (Omarchy) Kernel: 6.x Controller: Xbox Wireless Controller (Series X|S, USB‑C, Carbon Black) Dongle: Microsoft Xbox Wireless Adapter (045e:02fe) Desktop: Hyprland Games: Steam Controller Details Official product page:
https://www.xbox.com/en-US/accessories/controllers/xbox-wireless-controller-usb-c
Connection modes:
USB‑C (wired)
Xbox Wireless (2.4 GHz via official dongle)
The Problem Symptoms I hit:
Controller LED keeps blinking
Dongle visible in lsusb but will not pair
xow service crashes or restarts
Errors like:
Failed to load firmware
Firmware reset timed out
LIBUSB_ERROR_ACCESS
Sometimes the service looked active, but nothing actually worked.
Why This Happens xow is not a kernel driver.
It:
Runs in user space Talks to the dongle via libusb Uploads Microsoft firmware at runtime Emulates an Xbox controller for Linux input devices If firmware is missing or pairing order is wrong, the dongle stays unusable.
The Fix 1. Install xow git clone https://github.com/medusalix/xow.git cd xow make sudo make install 2. Install firmware (required) sed "s|@prefix@|/usr/local|g" install/firmware.sh.in > /tmp/xow-firmware.sh chmod +x /tmp/xow-firmware.sh sudo /tmp/xow-firmware.sh This installs:
/lib/firmware/xow_dongle.bin Verify:
ls -l /lib/firmware/xow_dongle.bin 3. systemd Service Configuration This is the working xow service file I ended up using.
[Unit] Description=Xbox One Wireless Dongle Driver [Service] Type=simple ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/xow Restart=on-failure Environment="XOW_COMPATIBILITY=1" [Install] WantedBy=multi-user.target Edit it with:
sudo SYSTEMD_EDITOR=nvim systemctl edit --full xow Enable and start:
sudo systemctl enable xow --now 4. Pair Using USB (Important) For Xbox Series X|S controllers, pairing once via USB is required.
Steps:
Plug controller using a USB‑C cable
Start xow
Wait for:
Dongle initialized Unplug the USB cable
Press pairing button on:
Dongle
Controller
After this, wireless pairing works normally.
Verify journalctl -u xow shows:
Dongle initialized
Pairing enabled
Controller LED becomes solid
Steam detects an Xbox Controller
Games receive input
Lessons Learned The official Xbox dongle requires firmware (xow or xone) xow is a user‑space USB translator, not a kernel driver USB pairing once is necessary for Series X|S controllers Linux exposes complexity that Windows hides TL;DR Install xow Install firmware Enable service Pair once via USB Use wireless after References xow: https://github.com/medusalix/xow Xbox Controller: https://www.xbox.com/en-US/accessories/controllers/xbox-wireless-controller-usb-c
summary: Using Xbox controller with official USB dongle required runtime firmware and user-space darmon called xow.
title: Fixing Xbox Series X|S Controller with official Dongle on Arch Linux (Omarchy)
